item_definition.name: Electronic Brake-by-Wire (BBW) & Regenerative Braking Subsystem
item_definition.system_boundary: Function-level boundary encompassing the complete braking signal chain: from the physical Brake Pedal Sensor Unit (BPSU) and Vehicle Motion & Chassis Domain Controller (VDCM), through the Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM) and Regenerative Inverter Controller (RIC), down to the 4-corner Smart Electro-Mechanical Brake Caliper Actuators (EMBA). Includes the exposed OBD-II / Wireless Diagnostic Service Interface on the VDCM.

functions.name: Driver Pedal Travel Sensing
functions.description: Samples two redundant Hall-effect pedal travel sensors at 1 kHz in COMP-BPSU and transmits driver pedal demand over Chassis CAN-FD to COMP-VDCM.

functions.name: Brake Torque Blending & Dynamic Allocation
functions.description: Calculates total braking demand, coordinates regenerative torque with RIC, and sends the remaining friction torque request to EBCM.

functions.name: Electro-Mechanical Friction Brake Actuation
functions.description: EBCM calculates per-wheel clamping force commands from friction braking demand and wheel-slip control. Each EMBA converts its assigned command into motor actuation to press the brake pads against the rotor.

modeling_assumptions: This synthetic model describes the primary electronic braking path. Independent emergency braking paths are outside its scope; their availability must not be assumed.
Communication timeouts and the sensor-agreement tolerance are configurable. Their numeric calibration is outside this item definition.

components.name: Brake Pedal Sensor Unit (BPSU)
components.hardware: Infineon TLE4998S Hall Sensor + NXP S32K116 Cortex-M0+ MCU

hosted_software.name: pedal_feel_and_travel_encoder
hosted_software.role: Samples two redundant Hall-effect pedal travel sensors at 1 kHz and packages CAN ID 0x080 (Pedal_Travel_Demand)

operational_parameters.valid_demand_rule: Both sensor readings are within 0 to 100 percent inclusive and their absolute difference is within the configured agreement tolerance; pedal travel demand is their arithmetic mean and demand_valid is true
operational_parameters.invalid_demand_rule: If either reading is outside the permitted range or their absolute difference exceeds the configured tolerance, demand_valid is false; pedal_travel_percent has no meaning and neither sensor is selected as correct
operational_parameters.sensor_agreement_tolerance: Configured maximum difference between normalized travel readings
operational_parameters.pedal_demand_transmission: Send pedal demand and validity after each sensor sampling cycle, including when demand is invalid

physical_access.required_access: Cabin access and physical access to the BPSU board in the pedal box
physical_access.capability: Debugger access through the unlocked SWD header, including writes to pedal zero-point calibration storage

components.name: Vehicle Motion & Chassis Domain Controller (VDCM)
components.hardware: Renesas R-Car S4 (ARM Cortex-A55 + Cortex-R52 Lockstep)

hosted_software.name: bluez
hosted_software.role: BLE Factory & Workshop Wireless Brake Diagnostics Interface (Bleeding/Pad Service Mode)

hosted_software.name: mosquitto
hosted_software.role: Internal IPC / SOME-IP to MQTT Telemetry Bridge

hosted_software.name: brake_blending_coordinator
hosted_software.role: Calculates remaining friction torque demand from driver demand and achieved regenerative torque reported by RIC (CAN ID 0x1A0), then transmits SOME/IP BrakeTorqueRequest over TSN Ethernet to EBCM

operational_parameters.braking_torque_basis: Driver demand and reported regenerative contribution use the same torque basis, with positive values representing braking
operational_parameters.friction_torque_demand: max(0, driver demand - credited regenerative contribution)
operational_parameters.regen_feedback_acceptance: Accept correctly formatted CAN ID 0x1A0 feedback that passes E2E CRC-8; store reported torque and local monotonic reception time on each accepted message
operational_parameters.regen_feedback_on_invalid_message: Discard without updating stored torque or reception time; retain the previous contribution until timeout
operational_parameters.regen_feedback_on_timeout: When elapsed time since the last accepted message reaches the timeout, credit zero regenerative contribution and request the available driver demand through friction braking; if pedal demand is unavailable, its contribution remains zero
operational_parameters.regen_feedback_on_recovery: Resume blending with the reported torque from the next accepted message
operational_parameters.regen_feedback_timeout: Configured maximum time since the last accepted feedback message
operational_parameters.pedal_demand_acceptance: Accept correctly formatted CAN ID 0x080 with valid E2E CRC-8, demand_valid true, and travel within 0 to 100 percent inclusive; the last accepted message replaces the stored demand and its local monotonic reception time
operational_parameters.pedal_demand_timeout: Configured maximum time since the last accepted valid demand
operational_parameters.pedal_demand_on_invalid_or_missing: Retain the last accepted demand only until its timeout; invalid messages do not update demand or its reception time
operational_parameters.pedal_demand_on_timeout: Mark driver demand unavailable and set the pedal-derived braking demand to zero
operational_parameters.pedal_demand_on_recovery: Resume using the next accepted demand immediately; a valid zero-percent message releases pedal-derived demand immediately
operational_parameters.pedal_fallback_limitation: The hold-then-zero response is a simplified primary-path model, not a production safety strategy. Loss of valid pedal input can remove pedal-derived braking demand; independent fallback braking is not modeled.

hosted_software.name: regen_torque_inverter_app
hosted_software.role: Executes negative torque (regenerative braking) on traction motor and reports achieved regenerative torque to VDCM (CAN ID 0x1A0)

components.name: Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM)
components.hardware: NXP S32K344 (two ARM Cortex-M7 cores configured as one lockstep pair)

hosted_software.name: lwip
hosted_software.role: Embedded TCP/IP stack for the Ethernet interface

hosted_software.name: abs_esc_clamping_controller
hosted_software.role: Processes SOME/IP braking demand over lwIP, executes wheel-slip PID loop, and sends all four wheel clamping force values in each CAN-FD command frame (ID 0x040)

diagnostic_services.routine: Caliper piston retraction for pad replacement
diagnostic_services.execution_behavior: EBCM requests pad-service entry or explicit exit for the selected wheel actuators over the actuator bus
diagnostic_services.target_selection: The request identifies selected COMP-EMBA wheel instances

diagnostic_programming.image_activation_rule: Activate only complete compatible images whose signature verifies against a configured trusted firmware signer; reject incomplete, unsigned, or invalidly signed images
diagnostic_programming.older_image_policy: An older compatible image can be accepted after programming authorization if its signature is valid

components.name: Smart Electro-Mechanical Brake Caliper Actuator (EMBA x4)
components.hardware: CAN-FD-capable automotive MCU with an external 48V-rated three-phase BLDC motor-driver stage; specific parts not selected

hosted_software.name: caliper_piston_servo_driver
hosted_software.role: Drives 48V BLDC ball-screw mechanism to push brake pads against disc rotor using only the clamping force field assigned to its wheel instance in CAN ID 0x040

security_configuration.wheel_harness_physical_shielding: Unshielded wheel-well twisted pair (accessible without cabin entry)

operational_parameters.command_force_range: Zero to the configured maximum clamping force
operational_parameters.command_acceptance: Accept a correctly formatted CAN ID 0x040 frame when the assigned wheel value is within the configured force range; the last accepted value becomes the force target and updates local monotonic reception time
operational_parameters.command_timeout: Configured maximum time since the last accepted command
operational_parameters.on_invalid_command: Reject without changing the force target or refreshing the command timer
operational_parameters.on_command_timeout: Record a communication fault and retain the last accepted force target
operational_parameters.on_command_recovery: Resume tracking the next accepted command and clear the communication fault
operational_parameters.force_control: The servo regulates force under the active motor-current limit; retaining a force target does not command continuous maximum motor current
operational_parameters.command_processing_scope: The normal-command acceptance and timeout rules apply in normal mode; pre-service normal commands are not restored after pad-service exit

pad_service_mode.entry: On an EBCM pad-service entry request targeting this instance, retract the piston to its configured service position
pad_service_mode.normal_command_priority: Normal CAN ID 0x040 commands do not change the target in pad-service mode and are not saved for use after exit
pad_service_mode.completion: Remain in pad-service mode after retraction completes until an explicit service-exit request
pad_service_mode.exit: Restore normal command processing and discard the pre-service normal target and reception time; wait at the service position for the next newly accepted 0x040 command
pad_service_mode.other_instances: Actuators not targeted by the request continue their existing operation

connections.name: Workshop BLE & OBD-II Diagnostic Interface
connections.medium: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE 5.0) & Physical OBD-II Port (ISO 15765-4)
connections.authenticated: BLE diagnostic service requires pairing with fixed passkey 000000; OBD-II requires physical connection. VDCM UDS 0x2F requires no additional application authorization.

entry_points.protocol: Workshop diagnostic requests over GATT / L2CAP
entry_points.access_requirement: Wireless proximity and pairing with the fixed six-digit passkey 000000 for normal diagnostic service access
Physical connection to the diagnostic connector; no additional client authentication for the VDCM brake override service

downstream_routes.request_scope: Forward EBCM-supported diagnostic requests; EBCM applies authorization for each operation

connections.name: Chassis & Pedal Sensor CAN-FD Bus
connections.protocol: Raw CAN-FD Frames (CAN ID 0x080 Pedal Travel, CAN ID 0x1A0 Regen Torque Status)

payload_fields.name: pedal_travel_percent
payload_fields.meaning: Arithmetic mean of the two sensor readings when demand_valid is true; no meaning when demand_valid is false

payload_fields.name: demand_valid
payload_fields.meaning: Result of the BPSU sensor range and disagreement checks

payload_fields.name: achieved_regenerative_torque
payload_fields.meaning: Braking torque the RIC reports it has delivered

connections.authenticated: None (CRC-8 error detection only; AUTOSAR SecOC disabled)

connections.name: Braking TSN Ethernet Link
connections.protocol: SOME/IP Service 0x1020 over UDP (configured application port on COMP-EBCM) & DoIP over TCP Port 13400
connections.authenticated: None (Plaintext SOME/IP without MACsec, IPsec, or SecOC)

connections.name: Wheel-End Brake Actuator CAN-FD Bus

messages.name: Target_Clamping_Force_kN
messages.receiver_behavior: Each actuator reads only the field assigned to its instance; hardware, software, interfaces, and security settings are shared through COMP-EMBA

connections.medium: Private CAN-FD Sub-bus routed to all 4 wheel wells (2 Mbps)
connections.protocol: Raw CAN-FD Frames (CAN ID 0x040 Target_Clamping_Force_kN) & UDS (0x750)
connections.authenticated: None (Plaintext CAN-FD without SecOC; physical wiring exposed in wheel arches)

physical_access.required_access: Physical contact with the CAN-FD wiring

assets.name: Driver Pedal Travel & Braking Demand Signal (CAN ID 0x080)

damage_scenarios.description: Insufficient braking during an emergency stop or unintended braking at highway speed can cause a collision. The collision can cause serious injury or death.

assets.name: Regenerative Torque Feedback and Friction Torque Request (CAN ID 0x1A0 and SOME/IP 0x1020)

damage_scenarios.description: Insufficient combined regenerative and friction braking can prevent the vehicle from achieving the required deceleration. This can cause a collision and serious injury or death.

assets.name: Wheel Caliper Clamping Force Command (CAN ID 0x040)

damage_scenarios.description: Uneven or insufficient wheel braking can cause loss of directional control or increased stopping distance. This can cause a collision and serious injury or death.

Loss of anti-lock braking or damage to brake actuators can reduce braking performance and vehicle stability. This can cause a collision and serious injury or death. Damaged actuators can require replacement and prevent vehicle use.

external_actors.description: Sentinel endpoint in connections used for externally reachable links; not a component of the item.
